detail: the property is `readOnly` — the document says only responses carry it — and its type is reached from a request body, so the one generated type carries it on the way out too
the operation declares no `operationId`, so its method is named after its method and path; adding one to the document pins the name
another operation is already called `delete_integration`, so this one is called `delete_integration2`; the two are told apart by a suffix because nothing in the document tells them apart
`GET /api/users/invites/{token}` cannot be registered beside `/api/users/invites/{inviteId}`, which the router already matches; the generated server omits this operation and the client keeps it
`propertyNames` narrow which values are valid in a way no Rust type expresses; the generated type accepts more than the document allows
